t: You're in Connaught Square, the first square of city houses built in Bayswater. Its appearance is essentially the same as it was in the 1820s. It's named after the Duke of Gloucester and Edinburgh, Prince William Frederick, a nephew of George the Third who married the king's daughter Mary in 1816. He kept his fringe-of-London house and grounds on the land of this square and nearby Gloucester Square. The square hosts one other notable name: Sir Arthur Hetherington, the first chairman of British Gas, who died here.
